messages:
pagerduty: :rotating_light: PAGER: High error rate (5xx) + elevated tail latency observed for requests routed to eu-west for model 'llama-13b-q' starting ~08:10 UTC. Significant fallback traffic to variant 'llama-13b-q-7'. Some responses appear to be returning from the wrong model variant due to KV/cache reuse. Paging sre-oncall(AMER). Priority: P0.

sre-oncall(AMER): Ack — taking incident. Initial read: routing fallback + KV keying mismatch hypothesis. I'll pull routing logs and kv metrics.

carla (eng-runtime): I can confirm: router logs show served_variant != origin_variant for a subset of requests. KV hit rates are up for eu-west shards. Pulling logs for request_ids that show mismatch now.

carla (eng-runtime): snippet from logs (sanitized):
```
2026-02-18T08:11:02Z router[event] request_id=abc123 model=llama-13b-q origin_variant=v1 served_variant=v7 kv_hit=true
2026-02-18T08:11:02Z kv[euw] key=llama-13b-q::prefix::xyz owner_shard=12 returned_variant=v1
```

dmitri (runtime): Repro hypothesis: routing policy allowed cross-region fallback and our cache key only included model name+prefix, not variant or region-specific variant id. When fallback happened, the router served a different variant while the cache still returned responses produced by the original variant.

ben (prod): Customer impact: we've got 3 customer reports of garbled completions (one internal high-priority: AcmeInc on embeddings route). Support ticket escalated. No public status yet.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0342 created. Channel #inc-2026-0342 created for incident coordination.

sre-oncall(AMER): Immediate mitigations I'm going to apply now:
1) Disable cross-region fallback for model 'llama-13b-q' (eu-west) to stop variant mixing.
2) Flush KV entries matching 'llama-13b-q*' on eu-west KV shards.
3) Pin routing table for eu-west to prefer 'llama-13b-q-v1' for 30m.
Executing step 1+2 now — will post command output.

carla (eng-runtime): Commands I'm running: 
```bash
# disable cross-region fallback for this model in control plane
curl -s -X POST https://controlplane.internal/v1/routing/disable_fallback \
  -d '{"model":"llama-13b-q","region":"eu-west","reason":"variant-mismatch-p0"}'

# KV flush (pattern) - note: this will cause cold misses for a short window
redis-cli -h kv-eu-west-01 --scan --pattern 'llama-13b-q*' | xargs -r redis-cli -h kv-eu-west-01 del
```

carla (eng-runtime): KV flush started. Expect a short spike in origin latency while caches warm. Monitoring.

dmitri (runtime): I'll open an emergency PR to include variant id in the KV cache key and add a small TTL guard to avoid cross-variant reuse. PR link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/2345 (draft).

alice (platform): Drafting a status page update (internal first) and pinging support for customer comms. Will post a public update once we confirm mitigations.

ben (prod): Rolling back the canary change to routing policy 'prefer_cheapest_variant' that was flipped yesterday — that policy appears to be the trigger when combined with regional fallback. Rolling back now.

sre-oncall(AMER): After disable+flush: metrics look better — 5xx rate dropping, served_variant == origin_variant mismatch count down from ~120/min to ~3/min. Latency tail moving toward baseline. Continuing to monitor.

carla (eng-runtime): Patch PR for cache-key change includes tests and a migration plan to avoid cold-start storms (staggered rollouts). Assigning dmitri to push to canary after patch review.

ben (prod): Customer impact summary for on-call handoff:
- Affected model: llama-13b-q (embeddings + text routes)
- Symptom: garbled outputs + 5xx in some requests when fallback occurred
- Scope: approx 1.2% of global traffic hitting eu-west during 08:10-08:35 UTC; 3 escalations, 1 enterprise customer (AcmeInc) impacted
- Mitigation: disabled cross-region fallback for eu-west, flushed KV keys, pinned variant mapping, rolled back routing policy canary

sre-oncall(AMER): Handoff to next on-call (oncall-sre-2) in 30m. Summary for you, @oncall-sre-2:
- Incident: INC-2026-0342 (cache keying + routing fallback caused cross-variant reuse)
- Actions taken: disabled fallback (control plane), flushed eu-west KV keys, pinned variant mapping for 30m, rolled back routing policy canary
- Ongoing: monitor mismatch counters, ensure patch PR gets promoted to canary and then staged rollout. Watch for cold-miss spike after cache flush.
- Owners: dmitri -> runtime patch + canary rollout; carla -> validate KV metrics; ben -> customer comms; alice -> status page
- Important commands run (kept in incident log):
```
# control plane change
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/v1/routing/disable_fallback -d '{"model":"llama-13b-q","region":"eu-west"}'

# KV purge (ran on eu-west shard group)
redis-cli -h kv-eu-west-01 --scan --pattern 'llama-13b-q*' | xargs -r redis-cli -h kv-eu-west-01 del
```

oncall-sre-2: Ack. Taking on-call in 25m. I'll keep watch on mismatch_count and 5xx. If mismatch_count > 10/min or 5xx > baseline+0.5% escalate to eng-runtime.

dmitri (runtime): PR #2345 pushed to canary in eu-west staging. Initial tests look good — cache keys now include variant id. No regressions in throughput. Planning staged rollout across eu shards tomorrow.

carla (eng-runtime): Validation: mismatch_count at 08:40 UTC -> 1/min, 5xx back to baseline. KV hit-rate normalizing. Will continue to monitor for 2 hours.

alice (platform): Public status update drafted, waiting final confirmation. Internal support notified customers.

sre-oncall(AMER): Marking incident as mitigated at 08:45 UTC. We'll keep the incident channel open for postmortem notes. On-call handoff complete. If anything regresses, reopen pager and escalate. :white_check_mark:
